text:
Sasha: Pushed a 30s nsight capture from a Dedicated host that reproduces a latency spike pattern. Timeline shows repeated small H2D host memcpy bursts on a different CUDA stream that appear to serialize a low-latency kernel on the main stream. Posting a compact annotated excerpt.

Sasha: ```nsys timeline (annotated)
[0.000s] host memcpy (stream 2) 0.12ms
[0.125s] kernel: forward_layer (stream 0) 0.22ms
[0.350s] host memcpy (stream 2) 0.11ms
[0.475s] kernel: forward_layer (stream 0) 0.20ms  <-- 1.1ms gap before this due to CPU wake
[0.600s] host memcpy (stream 2) 0.14ms
[0.740s] kernel: forward_layer (stream 0) 0.19ms
```

Sasha: The pattern: small host copies interleaved with short kernels, but the kernel on stream 0 sometimes waits ~1ms. In several traces the copy shows up earlier in wall-clock but kernel starts late (CPU scheduling gap).

Mike: Interesting — looks like the copy is submitted from the batcher thread (stream 2) which is used for KV cache prewarm. If that thread gets preempted while doing the host staging, the H2D finishes late and the main-stream kernel stalls on a dependency/event.

Mike: Quick hypothesis: our prefetch path uses synchronous host memcpy on a pinned-pool thread; when the thread is preempted the `cudaMemcpyAsync` submission is delayed. Also the batcher currently uses the same priority for prefetch stream vs compute stream.

Devon: Can you paste the batcher prefetch config you ran with? Also we should capture `perf sched` around the same window to see CPU wakeups.

Sasha: Config snippet I used: ```yaml
batcher: 
  max_batch_size: 8
  kvcache_prefetch: true
  prefetch_threads: 2
  prefetch_mode: synchronous_host_copy
```

Sasha: Repro command I used: `./tools/run_trace.sh --nsys --capture=30 --qps=200 --batch=8 --kvcache=on`

Mike: Try switching `prefetch_mode` to `async_host_copy` and submit prefetch copies on a dedicated low-latency stream with higher priority. Also set `prefetch_concurrency: 4` so copies are staggered. Example change: ```yaml
batcher:
  kvcache_prefetch: true
  prefetch_mode: async_host_copy
  prefetch_stream_priority: high
  prefetch_concurrency: 4
```

Mike: If that reduces the wait hotspots in nsight, it points to CPU submit latency being root cause rather than device-side copy contention.

Devon: I'll collect a short perf trace around the same run. Command: `sudo perf record -e sched:sched_wakeup -a -g -- sleep 35` then `perf script` for the window. Also get `ps -eo pid,comm,rtprio,ni,psr` on repro machine.

perf-bot: FYI — I scanned the node and saw occasional high iowait spikes correlated with backups at 03:00 UTC. Might be noisy.

Sasha: Good call. One more oddity: some of the kernels show tiny grid launches (~128 threads) and very short lifetime — the kernel scheduler overhead becomes non-trivial at high QPS. We might reduce kernel launch count by microbatching a bit and relying on KV cache to serve prefix hits.

Mike: For diagnostics, capture two nsight runs: (A) current config, (B) `prefetch_mode=async_host_copy` + `prefetch_stream_priority=high`. Compare `CUDA API` submission times vs `CUDA Runtime` kernel start times in the timeline. If submit->start delta reduces in B, we win.

Devon: I'll run both tonight and upload traces to /mnt/traces/2410032100/. Also will attach perf sched output.

Sasha: After that, if it repros, propose a small change: move prefetch submission off the batcher main thread into a lightweight io thread that only enqueues `cudaMemcpyAsync` + records an event. That reduces chance of preemption delaying submissions.

Mike: Agreed. Also consider switching hostcopy to use our pinned-copy pool with `cudaHostRegister` for transient buffers; reduces page-migration jitter.

Devon: Next steps checklist: 1) run diagnostic nsys A/B, 2) run perf sched capture, 3) test async prefetch config, 4) if improved, prototype io-thread submit change. I'll post links when done.

Sasha: Thanks — tagging @Mike and @Devon for follow-up. :thumbsup:
